newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee retreats, Sept ends shy of $1,600.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee retreats, Sept ends shy of $1,600.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures stepped back from an early uptrend to finish Thursday at the day's floor on aggressive trade selling towards the close, traders said.
September and November led the decline, each losing $23 to end at $1,597 and $1,587 per tonne respectively.
Both positions started the day in the plus column in what was seen as an attempt to consolidate overnight gains after rebounding from steep losses a day earlier.

September hit a ceiling at $1,645, up $25 on the day. But the rise proved short-lived as the market soon reversed to break below the $1,620 level when trade selling escalated. The contract saw a five-month low of $1,530 on Wednesday.
No fresh fund or speculative involvement was seen.
Thursday's fall was also probably exaggerated by a lack of volume. The day's tally stood at just 2,805 lots, led by September.
"It's a calm after the storm," said one trader. "The funds are waiting to see how the charts move again."
Technically the market might rise slightly if September regained its grip above the five-day moving average of $1,697. "But I doubt we could achieve it this week," one analyst said.
There were no fresh news, with players keeping a watchful eye on the Brazilian weather for this weekend.
Private U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp said in its latest report no damaging cold was in sight for the next five days in the coffee areas.
Brazilian meteorologists Somar also said no risk of damaging cold was seen in the next five days, with any polar air masses all passing through the far south of the country.
Minimum temperaturs should remain between 10 and 17 degress Celsius, Somar said.
The last crop-damaging frosts in Brazil were in late June and early July 1994.
